report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a professional culinary/recipe assistant (cooking domain, instructional/professional tone).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells overwhelmingly point to cooking/culinary concepts and actions: “Cook,” “Cooking,” “microwave,” “Baked,” “oven,” “baking,” “kitchen,” “restaurant,” “culinary,” “Chef/chef,” “Cake,” “Cooking,” “Kitchen.” This pattern repeats across many layers and positions (e.g., L21–L25, pos1–pos4).
- The same cells also strongly favor “professional/Professional,” “technical/Technical,” “Engineering/engineering,” and “professionalism,” indicating a formal, instructional, or trade/pro tone rather than casual food chatter—consistent with recipe steps, equipment use, and culinary-school/chef guidance.
- Earlier/mid-layer biases toward “dissertation,” “doctoral,” “Innovation,” “methodology,” and later “molecular” suggest a push toward formal/technical writing and even “molecular gastronomy”/culinary science vibes, reinforcing a precise, expert style within the cooking domain.
- The difference norms peak in later layers and across positions (especially pos1), which is characteristic of a high-level behavior/style/domain shift rather than a narrow lexical tweak.

Patchscope readouts were not provided here, but the logit-lens and norm patterns are strong and consistent with finetuning for professional cooking/recipe generation and culinary advice.
